title: Mobile (Expo Go + EAS Build)
description: Pair your phone in 30 seconds via Expo Go, or build a personal IPA for production-grade installation.

steps.title: Expo Go — instant phone pairing
steps.body:
Settings → Mobile. The first tab, **Try in Expo Go**, gets you on your phone in under a minute.

**On your phone:** install **Expo Go** from the App Store or Play Store (free). Open it. That's it.

**On the dashboard:** click Start Expo dev server. The QR code that appears encodes the connection.

steps.title: Tunnel vs LAN vs Localhost
steps.body:
Three connection modes:

- **Tunnel** — works anywhere (cellular, different Wi-Fi, behind NAT). Slower because traffic routes through Expo's servers. Recommended.
- **LAN** — same Wi-Fi only. Fastest because direct.
- **Localhost** — same machine only. Use for the iOS simulator or web preview.

Tunnel is the default. Switch only if you have a reason.

steps.title: Pre-baked credentials
steps.body:
Before starting Metro, the dashboard writes your gateway URL + your password to `<expoProject>/.env.local`. The Expo app reads these at boot — you never type them on your phone.

If your phone is on cellular and the gateway is on your laptop, you'll need a public URL (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, ngrok). Paste it into the **Gateway URL** field on the page; click Save default so the next start uses it.

steps.title: Scan the QR
steps.body:
**iOS:** open the Camera app, point at the QR. Tap the banner that appears. Expo Go opens with the app loaded.

**Android:** open Expo Go, tap **Scan QR code**, point at the QR.

The app boots, sees the env vars, connects to your gateway with your token. Done.

steps.title: What Expo Go can't do
steps.body:
Expo Go is the right call for trying things, demos, temporary access. But:

- **Push notifications won't fire** — Apple requires the bundle id of a built app
- Native widgets / share extensions don't appear
- Background tasks pause when Expo Go is closed

When any of those matter, switch to the **Build my own IPA** tab.

steps.title: IPA build — prerequisites
steps.body:
Building a personal IPA requires three things, each one-time:

1. **Apple Developer account** — $99/year, signup at `developer.apple.com/programs`. Apple takes 24-48 hours to approve. There's no way around this if you want the app on your iPhone.
2. **Expo account** (free) at `expo.dev`.
3. **EAS CLI** installed: open a terminal, run `npm install -g eas-cli`, then `eas login`.

After that, run `eas credentials` once — pick iOS, follow the prompts, EAS auto-fetches certificates and provisioning profiles using your Apple ID.

steps.title: Kick the build
steps.body:
Settings → Mobile → **Build my own IPA** tab. Click **Build iOS Preview**. The build queues on Expo's servers and finishes in ~15-25 minutes.

Watch progress in the Recent Builds table — refresh button polls EAS for status. When it's done you get an email with a download QR; scan that on your iPhone, Safari handles the install.

First time only: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → tap your developer profile → Trust. Then the InfiniBot icon appears on your home screen.
